Perfume rating 4.18 out of 5 with 4,187 votes

Emporio Armani Lei by Giorgio Armani is a Oriental Floral fragrance for women. Emporio Armani Lei was launched in 1998. The nose behind this fragrance is Daniela Andrier. Top notes are Lime, Tuberose, Bergamot, Pear, Mandarin Orange and Pineapple; middle notes are Heliotrope, Orris Root, Jasmine and Lily-of-the-Valley; base notes are Sandalwood, Vanilla, Musk, Almond, Tonka Bean, Cedar and Amber.

mychinarose 08/23/25 09:55

I’m not exactly sure which bottle I have: this 2018 bottle of “Lei” or 2020’s “She” which means the same thing. My bottle is very heavy on the fresh lime smell and sandalwood, which at first don’t seem like they would go together well but they really do. Lei is a lot of people’s holy grail scent, apparently, and that’s why I blind bought it a few years ago. It’s so good. If you like unisex scents, this is great. It actually smells a lot like lotion, like your old school Eucerin or something, but with a fresh kick from the lime. I was searching my collection today for something to wear in the heat that wasn’t too sweet that might give me a headache, but that still smelled fresh and summery. While Lei doesn’t have any coconut notes, it’s definitely in the same family as KKW Body II, or Guerlain Coconut Fizz…but with lime replacing the coconut. The heliotrope and orris give it the creamy lotion edge to it. Does it knock my socks off? No. But it’s a great signature scent if you want a daily wear fragrance.

I like it, but I really do wish it was stronger! The underbody is so weak, it makes such a little point to wear :(. Armani come back to us make an intense version.

LuckyLei 04/27/24 23:05

I love 'Lei' this is the original and best version. I think it's irreplaceable just like the OG Emporio White for her was. I used to buy them together, White for day wear and Lei for evenings.

Don't know if this is helpful or not but with regards to this fragrance's reformulation, I did some detective work using Fragrantica as the only reference, so it may not be gospel.
This fragrance has had three iterations.
Emporio Armani 'Lei' for Women was the original version launched in 1998 in the brushed champagne gold tube and presented in that unique sealed champagne gold packet.

In 2008 it was reformulated and relaunched as "For Her' with the words 'lei' and 'she' printed in black on the tube, which was a metallic gold tone, as opposed to the former brushed 'champagne' tone of gold. The 'lime' and 'tuberose' had been removed from the opening, two flowers swapped out in the heart and the base was stripped back to three notes, leaving out the 'tonka bean', 'sandalwood', 'almond' and 'amber'.

The third iteration launched in 2020 returns in the brushed champagne gold tube and is boxed instead of in the cute packet of the original.
The formulation appears to be a little closer to the original. The base is a little more filled out but still missing 'tonka bean' and 'sandalwood'. The heart has a couple of flowers swapped again and the top is missing 'pineapple', 'tuberose' and not sure if there's any 'mandarin, bergamot or lime' as the new formulation just says 'citrus notes' which may or may not include some of those.

After analyzing each note that was removed or swapped, I'm more hopeful this most recent version restored the vibe of what I personally loved about the original fragrance.

UPDATE: I ended up purchasing the latest formulation. On my skin the opening notes are not harmonizing, the dry down is linear, the heart notes are indistinct and watery and although the final skin scent is closely reminiscent of the original, it's missing the creamy milky sandalwood and sophisticated tobacco note of the tonka bean. In my opinion 'Lei' was sultry and sexier.

Yet the brushed champagne gold tube holds nostalgia and remnants of that soft fluffy skin scent, so I'll keep persisting. Perhaps I'll discover more to like?
If you loved the original 'Lei' or 'For Her' I recommend testing before buying to avoid disappointment.

I did not realize this was discontinued! I’m on my second or third bottle since it came out in 1998—definitely one of my top go-tos of all time. I don’t reach for it as often as I once did, but I do love having it in my arsenal for when the mood strikes.

This was a revolutionary fragrance when it first came out, the inspiration for lots of less expensive knockoffs, including Victoria’s Secret Dream Angels Heavenly, which came very close, but this one is top notch—the blending and quality can’t be matched by any of its cheap imitators.

Recently I sampled Heeley’s Iris de Nuit and Dior’s Bois d’Argent. I found both strikingly similar to Lei, so I will probably turn to one of those when I find my bottle is empty. I can’t say they are identical, but they hit the mark just fine with my chemistry.

A nice 90s scent that makes for a unique choice in the present! Starts off with an aromatic kick that can be thought of as unisex or even masculine, and settles down into a fresh and creamy scent that becomes close to the skin near the end. Reminds me of a body cream, probably Nivea. It seems to fall in line with the 90s trend of unisex fragrances even though this is marketed towards women. I would not recommend this as a blind buy but I think it would be enjoyed by those who like to wear other fragrances like this.

Similar to Shea from The Body Shop, except Shea is nuttier and heavier which makes it a little too much for me sometimes. Armani Lei is lighter and fresher, I think it is possible in theory to wear it in warm weather but I haven't tried it in summer heat yet. Does anybody know if Diesel Plus Plus is comparable as well? @Yessamin: No, they're not the same perfume, in fact, one has nothing to do with the other. I learned this the hard way as I bought She thinking it was Lei, what a deception.

When I smelled Lei back many years ago, I thought it was the rarest, most enigmatic perfume I had ever come across. It was strange but in a very intriguing, addictive way. Like someone here very well said, it was the fragrance for the overachiever, the office girl who is a yuppie, has a sports car and is ruthless about her fast paced job. It smells like someone who has money, young money, like the Armani models in a glass framed/sunglasses advertisement at your eye doctor's office. I found it ver woody, but oh so unique, I wanted it.

In contrast, She is the total opposite. It's easy going, friendly, not a "Here I am" fragrance. I bought it by mistake thinking I was buying the unmistakable Lei powerhouse. What a deception. Don't get me wrong though, it is a very nice perfume, more on the soft, sweet side.

Lei is a smart, fast ranking young boss, and She is the new, inexperienced administrative assistant who is innocent in nature.

As other reviewers have stated, this is the perfect anyone, anytime, anywhere fragrance. Perfectly unisex, ageless, and just the right amount of sillage - people will smell it, but it will never offend. The only time I think this might not work is in the dog days of summer… but then again, I could be wrong. On my skin this wears very sandalwood heavy with a bit of citrus. Not overly sweet. The bottle itself is worth buying the fragrance. Such a beautiful design, minimal but so elegant and futuristic. The aluminium bottle is presented in the most beautiful champagne brushed gold and it's a real piece of art. The perfume box's packaging is also very nicely done and very unique. Italian design, of course, beats everything.

When it comes to the scent, it's very casual, but at the same time, a very elegant representation of its era (late 90s). There are no surprises there and I feel that this fragrance was created with the aim to be universally liked. I haven't found any person who hates this. Some people are indifferent towards it, but no one actually hates it. It's a very tasteful creation and I think that Giorgio Armani probably invested more effort into the bottle's design than the scent itself, which is great because if this fragrance had been marketed in a different bottle (for instance the extremely generic bottles that dominated today's commercial and niche market), it would've been easily forgettable.

Oh, how I miss the 90s and early 2000s when the companies actually invested in perfume as a whole, and not just the scent. We rarely see great design in perfume bottles anymore, every bottle seems to be a copy of the original Chanel crystal bottle, especially in the niche market, and it gets tiring.

This perfume has no projection whatsoever, but it gives you amazing personal experience. corkscrewcurly 12/28/18 23:47

@scarlett.angel

I've just read your comments below and will try to help, if I can.

I have this perfume and have just inspected the bottle. Whilst it looks perfectly plain at first glance, the name of the perfume is imprinted in the metal on the side of the bottle, around the bottom. If you enlarge the picture at the top of the page, you can - JUST - see it.

There are details (name of manufacturer, where it was made etc.) imprinted in the plastic at the bottom of the bottom of the bottle as well. There is also a code stamped here (on mine, it's 62N401). I've checked this code on checkcosmetic.net, which dates my bottle to April 2016.

I just applied some Kiehl's Original Musk to my wrists and breathed it in deeply, so this is probably not the best time to be sniffing another perfume... but I've spritzed Lei on a piece of paper. Although it's not what I'd describe as a powerful perfume, it's still clearly discernible, despite the Kiehl's (which also has had the benefit of the warmth from my skin) full frontal assault on my nose.

I'd describe Lei as being a warm, powdery, vanillic heliotrope perfume (I can't smell tuberose at all, but that seems to be a minor note, according to people anyway). I can smell the perfume from the paper from a reasonable distance - it certainly doesn't need to be right under your nose to be smelled, although it's definitely not a powerhouse.

My bottle is a couple of years old, so the packaging etc. may have been changed - but I would still expect the name of the manufacturer to be visible somewhere. I also think that the country it was made HAS to be on it, by EU law (although I'm happy to be corrected).

Linda JK 09/12/17 20:33

As someone else pointed out, this fragrance truly has stood the test of time. I was beyond excited when I found it after thinking it had been discontinued.

I used this in the late 90s/early 2000s and completely fell in love with it the first time I wore it. It was among the first fragrances I collected when I discovered my passion for perfumes at a young age.

I've worn this fragrance everywhere, at any time of day, and throughout the year. It's pretty adaptable, as angelfishie said, and always draws compliments.

I'm only now realizing that Sophie Labbe is the nose behind this fragrance. She's the nose behind several others I love/have tested/own/want.

I have always been very wary of fragrances that contain lime/lemon in them, as well as those described as "powdery". Lime/lemon do not work well with my body chemistry and *some* powdery scents simply don't work for me. There's something about them that I find offensive and somewhat sickening.

This fragrance does smell powdery, especially after it's dried down, but it's a lovely, soft, clean, creamy, and warm-ish powdery scent. For lack of a better word, EA Lei is simply endearing.

The blending of the notes in this fragrance is just so well done. There isn't one note that's screeching or overpowering (for me, anyway). The notes that would ordinarily come off tart/sharp (lime, pineapple, mandarin orange, bergamot) are balanced by everything else, particularly in the base notes.

If you use a heavy hand, you'll likely find this strong enough to cause a headache or bother those around you who are sensitive to perfumes. Use a light hand and the fragrance will leave a clean, soft trail.

If you are very conservative with it, someone would have to stand at least at arms' length to smell the scent, which is not a bad thing. The projection will be soft and clean enough to be really pleasant to the person smelling it.

I love this fragrance and plan to buy some more in case it disappears.

Emporio Lei is the perfect go-to scent for me. There's hardly a day when I'm just not in the mood for it, and it never fails to make me feel simultaneously alluring and clean. The real beauty is in the heart and the drydown. It just screams (or sings) 'class'

It projects to where I can be proud knowing that I smell sublime when people are next to me, but not so much that I worry about offending anyone/everyone in the room.

It may not be as flashy or attention-grabbing as some of the others, and probably isn't for everyone. I don't get complimented on it quite as much as I feel it deserves but I'll be damned if it isn't one of the most wearable and comfortable scents I've ever owned... and yet somehow it excites me. It will forever be a staple of my wardrobe.

LuckyLei 04/27/24 23:05

I love 'Lei' this is the original and best version. I think it's irreplaceable just like the OG Emporio White for her was. I used to buy them together, White for day wear and Lei for evenings.

Don't know if this is helpful or not but with regards to this fragrance's reformulation, I did some detective work using Fragrantica as the only reference, so it may not be gospel.
This fragrance has had three iterations.
Emporio Armani 'Lei' for Women was the original version launched in 1998 in the brushed champagne gold tube and presented in that unique sealed champagne gold packet.

In 2008 it was reformulated and relaunched as "For Her' with the words 'lei' and 'she' printed in black on the tube, which was a metallic gold tone, as opposed to the former brushed 'champagne' tone of gold. The 'lime' and 'tuberose' had been removed from the opening, two flowers swapped out in the heart and the base was stripped back to three notes, leaving out the 'tonka bean', 'sandalwood', 'almond' and 'amber'.

The third iteration launched in 2020 returns in the brushed champagne gold tube and is boxed instead of in the cute packet of the original.
The formulation appears to be a little closer to the original. The base is a little more filled out but still missing 'tonka bean' and 'sandalwood'. The heart has a couple of flowers swapped again and the top is missing 'pineapple', 'tuberose' and not sure if there's any 'mandarin, bergamot or lime' as the new formulation just says 'citrus notes' which may or may not include some of those.

After analyzing each note that was removed or swapped, I'm more hopeful this most recent version restored the vibe of what I personally loved about the original fragrance.

UPDATE: I ended up purchasing the latest formulation. On my skin the opening notes are not harmonizing, the dry down is linear, the heart notes are indistinct and watery and although the final skin scent is closely reminiscent of the original, it's missing the creamy milky sandalwood and sophisticated tobacco note of the tonka bean. In my opinion 'Lei' was sultry and sexier.

Yet the brushed champagne gold tube holds nostalgia and remnants of that soft fluffy skin scent, so I'll keep persisting. Perhaps I'll discover more to like?
If you loved the original 'Lei' or 'For Her' I recommend testing before buying to avoid disappointment.
